ambiguity.issue: Table 2 lists the allowed types for testcases without port, default and timer; the prohibition is implied by omission. Chosen reading: omission means prohibition (consistent with clause 5.4.1.1 restriction l).
readings: A formal parameter of a testcase SHALL NOT be of a port, default or timer type.
Table 2 is not exhaustive; other types may be allowed for testcase formal parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:signature
requirements.canonical: A signature IS not listed in table 2 because a signature declares parameters only.
requirements.original: NOTE: Signatures are not shown in the table, because a signature declares parameters only.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A template of a signature CAN be parameterized.
requirements.original: The templates for the signatures can be parameterized, however.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-parameter
requirements.canonical: The lazy or fuzzy property of a formal parameter IS valid only in the scope where the name of the parameter is visible.
requirements.original: Lazy and fuzzy properties are valid only in the scope, where the parameters' names are visible.

requirements.subject: ent:fuzzy-parameter
requirements.condition: a fuzzy parameter is passed to a formal parameter declared without `@lazy` or `@fuzzy`
requirements.canonical: If a fuzzy formal parameter is passed as actual parameter to a formal parameter declared without a modifier, the parameter IS NOT fuzzy inside the called function.
requirements.original: For example, if a fuzzy parameter is passed to a formal parameter declared without a modifier, it loses its fuzzy feature inside the called function.

requirements.subject: ent:fuzzy-parameter
requirements.condition: a fuzzy parameter is passed to a formal parameter declared `@lazy`
requirements.canonical: If a fuzzy formal parameter is passed as actual parameter to a lazy formal parameter, the parameter IS lazy inside the called function.
requirements.original: Similarly, if it is passed to a lazy formal parameter, it becomes lazy within the called function.

ambiguity.issue: 'it' (via 'Similarly') most likely refers to the fuzzy parameter of the preceding sentence; it could also be read as applying to any parameter passed on to a lazy formal parameter.
readings: A fuzzy formal parameter passed to a lazy formal parameter IS lazy within the called function.
Any formal parameter (lazy, fuzzy or without modifier) passed to a lazy formal parameter IS lazy within the called function.

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.canonical: A value of any basic type, any user-defined type, the address type, a component type, a port type, the timer type or the default type MAY be passed as a value parameter.
requirements.original: Values of all basic and user-defined types, address, component, port and timer types, and the default type can be passed as value parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter has the syntax [ ( `in` | `inout` | `out` ) ] [ ( `@lazy` | `@fuzzy` ) [ `@deterministic` ] ] TypeOrNestedTypeDef ValueParIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] [ ":=" ( Expression | "-" ) ].
requirements.original:
[ ( in | inout | out ) ] [ ( @lazy | @fuzzy ) [@deterministic] ] 
  TypeOrNestedTypeDef ValueParIdentifier [ArrayDef] [ ":=" ( Expression | "-" ) ]

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter CAN be used within the parameterized object in the same way as a value, e.g. in expressions.
requirements.original: Value formal parameters can be used within the parameterized object the same way as values, for example in expressions.

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter MAY be an in, inout or out parameter.
requirements.original: Value formal parameters may be in, inout or out parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.condition: no `in`, `inout` or `out` keyword is given
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter without a parameterization keyword IS an in parameter.
requirements.original: The default for value formal parameters is in parameterization which may optionally be denoted by the keyword in.

requirements.subject: ent:in-keyword
requirements.canonical: The in parameterization of a formal value parameter MAY optionally be denoted by the keyword `in`.
requirements.original: The default for value formal parameters is in parameterization which may optionally be denoted by the keyword in.

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.canonical: An inout or out formal value parameter SHALL be specified by the keyword `inout` or `out` respectively.
requirements.original: Using of inout or out kind of parameterization shall be specified by the keywords inout or out respectively.

requirements.subject: ent:in-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal in value parameter MAY have a default value, given by an expression assigned to the parameter.
requirements.original: In parameters may have a default value, which is given by an expression assigned to the parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:modified-template
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter of a modified template MAY inherit the default value of the corresponding parameter of its parent template.
requirements.original: Formal parameters of modified templates may inherit the default values from the corresponding parameters of their parent templates; this shall explicitly be denoted by using a dash (don't change) symbol at the place of the modified template parameters' default value.

requirements.subject: ent:dash-symbol
requirements.canonical: Inheritance of a default value by a formal parameter of a modified template SHALL be denoted explicitly by the dash (don't change) symbol in place of the default value.
requirements.original: Formal parameters of modified templates may inherit the default values from the corresponding parameters of their parent templates; this shall explicitly be denoted by using a dash (don't change) symbol at the place of the modified template parameters' default value.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.condition: a function is used to initialize the default value
requirements.canonical: If a function is used for the initialization of a default value of an in parameter, side effects SHOULD be avoided during the evaluation of the default value.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: If functions are used for the initialization of default values of in parameters, it is strongly advised to avoid side effects during the evaluation of default values.

requirements.subject: ent:side-effect
requirements.canonical: A side effect during the evaluation of a default value CAN cause non-deterministic test executions.
requirements.original: Side effects may cause non-deterministic test executions.

requirements.subject: ent:side-effect
requirements.canonical: A side effect during the evaluation of a default value CAN be avoided, e.g. by adhering to the rules of clause 16.1.4.
requirements.original: They can be avoided, e.g. by adhering to the rules defined in clause 16.1.4.

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.canonical: A module supports static value parameterization to support test suite parameters.
requirements.original: the language element module allows static value parameterization to support test suite parameters, i.e. this parameterization may or may not be resolvable at compile-time but shall be resolved by the commencement of runtime (i.e. static at runtime).

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: The value of a module parameter MAY be unresolvable at compile-time.
requirements.original: the language element module allows static value parameterization to support test suite parameters, i.e. this parameterization may or may not be resolvable at compile-time but shall be resolved by the commencement of runtime (i.e. static at runtime).

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: The value of a module parameter SHALL be resolved by the commencement of runtime.
requirements.original: the language element module allows static value parameterization to support test suite parameters, i.e. this parameterization may or may not be resolvable at compile-time but shall be resolved by the commencement of runtime (i.e. static at runtime).

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: At runtime, a module parameter value IS globally visible.
requirements.original: This means that, at runtime, module parameter values are globally visible but not changeable (see more details in clause 8.2);

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: At runtime, a module parameter value SHALL NOT be changed.
requirements.original: This means that, at runtime, module parameter values are globally visible but not changeable (see more details in clause 8.2);

requirements.subject: ent:language-element
requirements.canonical: A template, testcase, altstep or function supports dynamic value parameterization.
requirements.original: the language elements template, testcase, `altstep and function support dynamic value` parameterization (i.e. this parameterization shall be resolved at runtime).

requirements.subject: ent:language-element
requirements.canonical: The dynamic value parameterization of a template, testcase, altstep or function SHALL be resolved at runtime.
requirements.original: the language elements template, testcase, `altstep and function support dynamic value` parameterization (i.e. this parameterization shall be resolved at runtime).

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: A component reference or a default reference IS handled as a value parameter.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Component and default references are also handled as value parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: For a formal parameter receiving a component reference, the corresponding component type IS the type of the formal parameter.
requirements.original: In the case of component references, the corresponding component type is the type of the formal parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: For a formal parameter receiving a default reference, the type `default` IS the type of the formal parameter.
requirements.original: In the case of default references the TTCN-3 type default is the type of the formal parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:language-element
requirements.canonical: A `const`, `var`, `timer`, `control`, `record of`, `set of`, `enumerated`, `port`, `component` or subtype definition, a `group` or an `import` SHALL NOT be parameterized.
requirements.original: a) Language elements which cannot be parameterized are: const, var, `timer, control,` `record` `of,` `set` `of, enumerated, port, component` and subtype definitions, group and import.

ambiguity.issue: The list names record of, set of and enumerated but not record, set or union type definitions, while clause 5.4.1.0 mentions structured types as parameterizable and table 2 lists none. Chosen reading: the listed elements are not parameterizable; the list says nothing about other type definitions.
readings: Only the listed language elements SHALL NOT be parameterized; record, set and union type definitions MAY be parameterized.
No type definition SHALL be parameterized; the list is only illustrative and table 2 is exhaustive.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter of a template SHALL be an in parameter.
requirements.original: b) Formal value parameters of templates, and of altsteps activated as defaults (see clause 20.5.2) shall always be in parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter of an altstep activated as a default SHALL be an in parameter.
requirements.original: b) Formal value parameters of templates, and of altsteps activated as defaults (see clause 20.5.2) shall always be in parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: A default value SHALL be provided only for a formal in parameter.
requirements.original: d) Default values can be provided for in parameters only.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The expression of the default value of a formal parameter SHALL be compatible with the type of the parameter.
requirements.original: e) The expression of formal parameter's default value has to be compatible with the type of the parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The expression of the default value of a formal parameter MAY be any expression that is well-defined at the beginning of the scope of the parameterized entity.
requirements.original: The expression may be any expression that is well-defined at the beginning of the scope of the parameterized entity, but shall not refer to other parameters of the same parameter list.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The expression of the default value of a formal parameter SHALL NOT refer to other parameters of the same parameter list.
requirements.original: The expression may be any expression that is well-defined at the beginning of the scope of the parameterized entity, but shall not refer to other parameters of the same parameter list.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The default value of a component type formal parameter SHALL be one of the special values `null`, `mtc`, `self` or `system`.
requirements.original: f) Default values of component type formal parameters shall be one of the special values null, mtc, self, or system.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The default value of a port type, timer type or default type formal parameter SHALL be the special value `null`.
requirements.original: g) Default values of port, timer or default type formal parameters shall be the special value null.

requirements.subject: ent:dash-symbol
requirements.canonical: The dash (don't change) symbol SHALL be used only with formal parameters of modified templates.
requirements.original: h) The dash (don't change) symbol shall be used with formal parameters of modified templates only (see also clause 15.5).

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter of a template SHALL comply with the restrictions specified in clause 15.0.
requirements.original: i) For formal value parameters of templates the restrictions specified in clause 15.0 shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter declared `@lazy` or `@fuzzy` SHALL be an in parameter.
requirements.original: j) Only in parameters can be declared lazy or fuzzy.

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal value parameter is referenced
requirements.canonical: When a formal value parameter is referenced (e.g. in assignments, expressions or template bodies), the rules for variables SHALL apply.
requirements.original: k) When parameters are referenced (e.g. in assignments, expressions, template bodies, etc.), the rules for variables shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: Only a function or altstep definition SHALL have formal parameters of a port, timer or default type or of a type containing a direct or indirect element or field of a port, default or timer type.
requirements.original: l) Only function and altstep definitions with the exception of functions or altsteps started as test component behaviour (see clause 21.3.2) may have formal parameters of a port, timer or default type or of a type that contains a direct or indirect element or field of a port, default or timer type.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A function or altstep started as test component behaviour SHALL NOT have formal parameters of a port, timer or default type or of a type containing a direct or indirect element or field of a port, default or timer type.
requirements.original: l) Only function and altstep definitions with the exception of functions or altsteps started as test component behaviour (see clause 21.3.2) may have formal parameters of a port, timer or default type or of a type that contains a direct or indirect element or field of a port, default or timer type.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: Only a function, altstep or testcase definition SHALL have formal parameters of a component type or of a type containing a direct or indirect element or field of a component type.
requirements.original: m) Only function, altstep and testcase definitions may have formal parameters of a component type or of a type that contains a direct or indirect element or field of a component type.

requirements.subject: ent:deterministic-modifier
requirements.condition: the lazy or fuzzy value parameter is used in a deterministic context
requirements.canonical: If a lazy or fuzzy formal value parameter is used in a deterministic context (during the evaluation of a snapshot or the initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it SHALL be declared `@deterministic`.
requirements.original: n) If a lazy or fuzzy value parameter is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic.

requirements.subject: ent:template-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal template parameter IS used to pass a template into a parameterized object.
requirements.original: Template kind parameters are used to pass templates into parameterizable objects.

ambiguity.issue: 'template kind parameters' and 'parameterizable objects' deviate from the terms used elsewhere.

requirements.subject: ent:template-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal template parameter has the syntax [ `in` | `inout` | `out` ] TemplateModifier [ ( `@lazy` | `@fuzzy` ) [ `@deterministic` ] ] TypeOrNestedTypeDef ValueParIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] [ ":=" ( TemplateInstance | "-" ) ].
requirements.original:
[ in | inout | out ] TemplateModifier [ ( @lazy | @fuzzy ) [@deterministic] ]
  TypeOrNestedTypeDef ValueParIdentifier [ArrayDef] [ ":=" ( TemplateInstance | "-" ) ]

requirements.subject: ent:template-keyword
requirements.condition: the parameterized object shall accept templates or matching mechanisms as actual parameters
requirements.canonical: To accept templates or matching symbols as actual parameters, a formal parameter SHALL be declared with the keyword `template` before its type.
requirements.original: To enable a parameterized object to accept templates or matching symbols as actual parameters, the extra keyword `template` shall be added before the type field of the corresponding formal parameter.

ambiguity.issue: 'type field' and 'matching symbols' deviate from the usual terms; the syntax (TemplateModifier) also allows `omit` as shorthand instead of `template`.

requirements.subject: ent:template-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter declared with the keyword `template` IS a template parameter.
requirements.original: This makes the parameter a template parameter and in effect extends the allowed actual parameters for the associated type to include the appropriate set of matching attributes (see annex B) as well as the normal set of values.

requirements.subject: ent:template-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal template parameter accepts as actual parameters the matching mechanisms of annex B appropriate for its type as well as the values of its type.
requirements.original: This makes the parameter a template parameter and in effect extends the allowed actual parameters for the associated type to include the appropriate set of matching attributes (see annex B) as well as the normal set of values.

ambiguity.issue: 'matching attributes' is used where 'matching mechanisms' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:template-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal template parameter CAN be used within the parameterized object in the same way as a template or a template variable.
requirements.original: Formal template parameters can be used within the parameterized object the same way as templates and template variables.

requirements.subject: ent:template-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal template parameter MAY be an in, inout or out parameter.
requirements.original: Formal template parameters may be in, inout or out parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:template-parameter
requirements.condition: no `in`, `inout` or `out` keyword is given
requirements.canonical: A formal template parameter without a parameterization keyword IS an in parameter.
requirements.original: The default for formal template parameters is in parameterization.

requirements.subject: ent:in-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal in template parameter MAY have a default template, given by a template instance assigned to the parameter.
requirements.original: In parameters may have a default template, which is given by a template instance assigned to the parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:modified-template
requirements.canonical: A formal template parameter of a modified template MAY inherit the default template of the corresponding parameter of its parent template.
requirements.original: Formal template parameters of modified templates may inherit their default templates from the corresponding parameters of their parent templates; this shall explicitly be denoted by using a dash (don't change) symbol at the place of the modified template parameter's default template.

requirements.subject: ent:dash-symbol
requirements.canonical: Inheritance of a default template by a formal template parameter of a modified template SHALL be denoted explicitly by the dash (don't change) symbol in place of the default template.
requirements.original: Formal template parameters of modified templates may inherit their default templates from the corresponding parameters of their parent templates; this shall explicitly be denoted by using a dash (don't change) symbol at the place of the modified template parameter's default template.

requirements.subject: ent:default-template
requirements.condition: the default template is used
requirements.canonical: If a default template is used, it IS evaluated in the scope of the parameterized entity, not in the scope of the actual parameter list.
requirements.original: If a default template is used, it is evaluated in the scope of the parameterized entity, not the scope of the actual parameter list.

requirements.subject: ent:template-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal template parameter MAY be restricted to accept only actual parameters containing a restricted set of matching mechanisms.
requirements.original: Formal template parameters can be restricted to accept actual parameters containing a restricted set of matching mechanisms only.

requirements.subject: ent:template-restriction
requirements.canonical: A restriction of a formal template parameter IS expressed by `omit`, `present` or `value`.
requirements.original: Such limitations can be expressed by the restrictions omit, present, and value.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-restriction
requirements.canonical: The restriction `template (omit)` MAY be replaced by the shorthand notation `omit`.
requirements.original: The restriction template (omit) can be replaced by the shorthand notation omit.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A formal template parameter of a template SHALL be an in parameter.
requirements.original: b) Formal template parameters of templates and of altsteps activated as defaults (see clause 20.5.2) shall always be in parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: A formal template parameter of an altstep activated as a default SHALL be an in parameter.
requirements.original: b) Formal template parameters of templates and of altsteps activated as defaults (see clause 20.5.2) shall always be in parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:default-template
requirements.canonical: A default template SHALL be provided only for a formal in template parameter.
requirements.original: c) Default templates can be provided for in parameters only.

requirements.subject: ent:default-template
requirements.canonical: The default template instance of a formal template parameter SHALL be compatible with the type of the parameter.
requirements.original: d) The default template instance has to be compatible with the type of the parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:default-template
requirements.canonical: The default template instance of a formal template parameter MAY be any template expression that is well-defined at the beginning of the scope of the parameterized entity.
requirements.original: The template instance may be any template expression that is well-defined at the beginning of the scope of the parameterized entity, but shall not refer to other parameters in the same parameter list.

requirements.subject: ent:default-template
requirements.canonical: The default template instance of a formal template parameter SHALL NOT refer to other parameters in the same parameter list.
requirements.original: The template instance may be any template expression that is well-defined at the beginning of the scope of the parameterized entity, but shall not refer to other parameters in the same parameter list.

requirements.subject: ent:default-template
requirements.canonical: The default template of a component type formal template parameter SHALL be built from the special values `null`, `mtc`, `self` or `system`.
requirements.original: e) Default templates of component type formal parameters shall be built from the special values null, mtc,self, or system.

ambiguity.issue: 'built from' is unclear: it may require one of the four values, or allow any template (e.g. a value list) composed of them.
readings: The default template of a component type formal template parameter SHALL be one of `null`, `mtc`, `self` or `system`.
The default template of a component type formal template parameter MAY be any template (e.g. a value list or `?`-free combination) whose values are only `null`, `mtc`, `self` or `system`.

requirements.subject: ent:template-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal template parameter SHALL comply with the restrictions specified in clause 15.0.
requirements.original: f) Restrictions specified in clause 15.0 shall apply.

ambiguity.issue: Unlike clause 5.4.1.1 restriction i), which limits the rule to value parameters of templates, it is unclear whether this applies to all formal template parameters or only those of templates.
readings: A formal template parameter of any parameterized object SHALL comply with the restrictions of clause 15.0.
A formal template parameter of a template SHALL comply with the restrictions of clause 15.0.

requirements.subject: ent:dash-symbol
requirements.canonical: The dash (don't change) symbol SHALL be used only with formal template parameters of modified templates.
requirements.original: g) The dash (don't change) symbol shall be used with formal parameters of modified templates only (see also clause 15.5).

requirements.subject: ent:template-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal template parameter declared `@lazy` or `@fuzzy` SHALL be an in parameter.
requirements.original: h) Only in template parameters can be declared lazy or fuzzy.

requirements.subject: ent:template-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal template parameter is referenced
requirements.canonical: When a formal template parameter is referenced (e.g. in assignments, expressions or template bodies), the rules for template variables SHALL apply.
requirements.original: i) When template parameters are referenced (e.g. in assignments, expressions, template bodies, etc.), the rules for template variables shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:deterministic-modifier
requirements.condition: the lazy or fuzzy template parameter is used in a deterministic context
requirements.canonical: If a lazy or fuzzy formal template parameter is used in a deterministic context (during the evaluation of a snapshot or the initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it SHALL be declared `@deterministic`.
requirements.original: j) If a lazy or fuzzy template parameter is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: A value, template, timer or port MAY be passed into a parameterized TTCN-3 object as an actual parameter.
requirements.original: Values, templates, timers and/or ports can be passed into parameterized TTCN-3 objects as actual parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter-list
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter list MAY be given in list notation, with the actual parameters in the same order as the formal parameters.
requirements.original: Actual parameters can be provided both as a list in the same order as the formal parameters as well as in an assignment notation explicitly using the associated formal parameter names or in a mixed notation where the first parameters are given in list notation and additional parameters in assignment notation.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter-list
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter list MAY be given in assignment notation, explicitly using the names of the associated formal parameters.
requirements.original: Actual parameters can be provided both as a list in the same order as the formal parameters as well as in an assignment notation explicitly using the associated formal parameter names or in a mixed notation where the first parameters are given in list notation and additional parameters in assignment notation.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter-list
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter list MAY be given in mixed notation, where the first actual parameters are given in list notation and the additional actual parameters in assignment notation.
requirements.original: Actual parameters can be provided both as a list in the same order as the formal parameters as well as in an assignment notation explicitly using the associated formal parameter names or in a mixed notation where the first parameters are given in list notation and additional parameters in assignment notation.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter has the syntax ( Expression | TemplateInstance | "-" ) | ParameterId ":=" ( Expression | TemplateInstance | TimerRef | Port ), where "-" skips a parameter.
requirements.original:
( Expression | // for value parameter
   TemplateInstance |  // for template parameter
   "-" ) |  // to skip a parameter with default
   ParameterId ":=" ( Expression | TemplateInstance | TimerRef | Port ) )

ambiguity.issue: The syntax block has unbalanced parentheses, lists TimerRef and Port only for the assignment notation and does not list "-" in the assignment notation, although EXAMPLE 10 uses 'p_par1 := -'. Chosen reading: all alternatives are allowed in both notations.
readings: An actual parameter in list notation MAY be an Expression, a TemplateInstance, a timer reference, a port or "-", and in assignment notation ParameterId ":=" followed by any of these.
An actual parameter in list notation IS an Expression, a TemplateInstance or "-" only, and only the assignment notation allows TimerRef and Port, but not "-".

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the actual parameter is passed to an in formal value parameter
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter passed by value to an in formal value parameter SHALL be a variable, a literal value, a module parameter, a constant, a value variable, an invocation of a value returning function or external function, a formal value parameter (of in, inout or out parameterization) of the current scope, or an expression composed of these.
requirements.original: Actual parameters that are passed by value to in formal value parameters shall be variables, literal values, module parameters, constants, value variables, invocations of value returning (external) functions, formal value parameters (of in, inout or out parameterization) of the current scope or expressions composed of the above.

ambiguity.issue: The list contains both 'variables' and 'value variables'; it is unclear whether 'variables' includes template variables. Chosen reading: only value variables are meant.
readings: An actual parameter passed to an in formal value parameter SHALL NOT be a template variable.
An actual parameter passed to an in formal value parameter MAY be any variable, including a template variable, provided it evaluates to a value.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the actual parameter is passed to an out formal value parameter
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter passed to an out formal value parameter SHALL be a variable, a template variable, a formal value or template parameter (of in, inout or out parameterization), or a reference to an element of a variable, template variable or formal parameter of a structured type.
requirements.original: Actual parameters that are passed to out formal value parameters shall be (template) variables, formal (template) parameters (of in, inout or out parameterization) or references to elements of (template) variables or formal (template) parameters of structured types.

requirements.subject: ent:dash-symbol
requirements.canonical: The dash symbol "-" MAY be used as an actual parameter for an out formal value parameter.
requirements.original: Furthermore it is allowed to use the dash symbol "-" as an actual out parameter, signifying that a possible result for that parameter will not be passed back.

requirements.subject: ent:dash-symbol
requirements.canonical: When the dash symbol "-" is used as an actual out parameter, a possible result for that parameter IS NOT passed back.
requirements.original: Furthermore it is allowed to use the dash symbol "-" as an actual out parameter, signifying that a possible result for that parameter will not be passed back.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the actual parameter is passed to an inout formal value parameter
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter passed to an inout formal value parameter SHALL be a variable, a formal value parameter (of in, inout or out parameterization), or a reference to an element of a variable or formal value parameter of a structured type.
requirements.original: Actual parameters that are passed to inout formal value parameters shall be variables or formal value parameters (of in, inout or out parameterization) or references to elements of variables or formal value parameters of structured types.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element
requirements.canonical: A reference to a string element CANNOT be passed by reference, because string types are not structured types.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Reference to a string element cannot be passed by reference as string types are not structured types.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the actual parameter is passed to an in formal template parameter
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter passed to an in formal template parameter SHALL be a literal value, a module parameter, a constant, a variable, an invocation of a value or template returning function or external function, a formal value parameter (of in, inout or out parameterization) of the current scope, an expression composed of these, a template, a template variable, or a formal template parameter (of in, inout or out parameterization) of the current scope.
requirements.original: Actual parameters that are passed to in formal template parameters shall be literal values, module parameters, constants, variables, invocations of value or template returning (external) functions, formal value parameters (of in, inout or out parameterization) of the current scope or expressions composed of the above, as well as templates, template variables or formal template parameters (of in, inout or out parameterization) of the current scope.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the actual parameter is passed to an out formal template parameter
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter passed to an out formal template parameter SHALL be a template variable, a formal template parameter, or a reference to an element of a template variable or formal template parameter of a structured type.
requirements.original: Actual parameters that are passed to out formal template parameters shall be template variables, formal template parameters or references to elements of template variables or formal template parameters of structured types.

requirements.subject: ent:dash-symbol
requirements.canonical: The dash symbol "-" MAY be used as an actual parameter for an out formal template parameter.
requirements.original: Furthermore it is allowed to use the dash symbol "-" as an actual out parameter, signifying that a possible result for that parameter will not be passed back.

requirements.subject: ent:dash-symbol
requirements.canonical: When the dash symbol "-" is used as an actual parameter for an out formal template parameter, a possible result for that parameter IS NOT passed back.
requirements.original: Furthermore it is allowed to use the dash symbol "-" as an actual out parameter, signifying that a possible result for that parameter will not be passed back.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the actual parameter is passed to an inout formal template parameter
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter passed to an inout formal template parameter SHALL be a template variable or formal template parameter (of in, inout or out parameterization) of the current scope, or a reference to an element of a template variable or formal template parameter of a structured type.
requirements.original: Actual parameters that are passed to inout formal template parameters shall be template variables or formal template parameters (of in, inout or out parameterization) of the current scope or references to elements of template variables or formal template parameters of structured types.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the actual parameter is passed to an in formal parameter and contains a value or template reference
requirements.canonical: When an actual parameter passed to an in formal value or template parameter contains a value or template reference, the rules for using references on the right hand side of assignments SHALL apply.
requirements.original: When actual parameters that are passed to in formal value or template parameters contain a value or template reference, rules for using references on the right hand side of assignments apply.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the actual parameter is passed to an inout or out formal parameter and contains a value or template reference
requirements.canonical: When an actual parameter passed to an inout or out formal value or template parameter contains a value or template reference, the rules for using references on the left hand side of assignments SHALL apply.
requirements.original: When actual parameters that are passed to inout and out formal value or template parameters contain a value or template reference, rules for using references on the left hand side of assignments apply.

requirements.subject: ent:out-parameter
requirements.canonical: The values of out formal parameters ARE passed back to the actual parameters in the order of the formal parameters in the definition of the parameterized TTCN-3 object.
requirements.original: The values of out formal parameters are passed to the actual parameters in the same order as is the order of formal parameters in the definition of the parameterized TTCN-3 object.

requirements.subject: ent:out-parameter
requirements.canonical: The value of an out formal parameter IS passed back to the actual parameter only if a value is assigned to the out formal parameter within the invoked object.
requirements.original: The value is passed back to the actual parameter only if within the invoked object a value is assigned to it.

ambiguity.issue: 'it' may refer to the out formal parameter or to the actual parameter; the paragraph also does not say whether the rule covers inout parameters. Chosen reading: the out formal parameter.
readings: The value of an out formal parameter IS passed back to the actual parameter only if a value is assigned to the out formal parameter within the invoked object.
The value IS passed back to the actual parameter only if within the invoked object a value is assigned to the actual parameter (e.g. through a component variable or another reference).

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: no value is assigned to the out formal parameter
requirements.canonical: If no value is assigned to an out formal parameter within the invoked object, the corresponding actual parameter remains unchanged when the invoked object completes.
requirements.original: If no value is assigned, the actual parameter remains unchanged when the invoked object completes.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: An element of a structured value or template (record, set, record of, set of, union and anytype values or templates) MAY be passed by reference as an actual parameter.
requirements.original: It is allowed to pass elements of structured values or templates (record, set, record of, set of, union and anytype values or templates) by reference.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: Modification of a formal parameter to which an element of a structured value or template is passed by reference modifies the original structured value or template.
requirements.original: Modification of parameters passed this way affects the original structured value or template.

ambiguity.issue: 'parameters passed this way' does not say whether the formal or the actual parameter is modified.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: Before an element of a structured value or template is passed by reference, the rules for referencing the element on the left hand side of assignments ARE applied, expanding the structured value so that the referenced element becomes accessible.
requirements.original: Before passing the actual parameter, the rules for referencing the element on the left hand side of assignments are applied, expanding the structured value so that the referenced element becomes accessible (see clauses 6.2 and 15.6 for more details).

requirements.subject: ent:inout-parameter
requirements.canonical: Passing a part of a structured component variable as an actual inout parameter CAN have confusing effects, because changing either the inout formal parameter or the component variable can also change the other.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Because inout parameters are passed by reference and component variables are effectively also accessed by reference within a called function or altstep, passing parts of a structured component variable as an actual inout parameter may have confusing effects inside the parameterized behaviour: changing either the inout parameter or the component variable may also change the other simultaneously, which might break the intended algorithm.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: A part of a structured component variable SHOULD NOT be passed as an actual inout parameter to a function or altstep that accesses that component variable.
requirements.original: For this reason, such situations should be avoided.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal parameter is an out parameter or has a default value or template
requirements.canonical: If a formal parameter is an out parameter or has been defined with a default value or template, an actual parameter NEED NOT be provided for that formal parameter.
requirements.original: When a formal parameter is an out parameter or has been defined with a default value or template, respectively, then it is not necessary to provide an actual parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.condition: no actual parameter is provided for the formal parameter
requirements.canonical: If no actual parameter is provided for a formal parameter with a default value or template, the default value or template IS taken as the actual parameter.
requirements.original: In such a case the default value or template is taken as actual parameter.

ambiguity.issue: 'In such a case' follows a sentence that also covers out parameters without a default value, which have no default to take. Chosen reading: the rule applies to formal parameters with a default; out parameters without default behave as if "-" was given (see the following paragraph).
readings: If no actual parameter is provided for a formal parameter with a default value or template, the default value or template IS taken as the actual parameter.

If no actual parameter is provided for an out parameter or a formal parameter with default, the default value or template IS taken as the actual parameter, and an out parameter without default has no actual parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: The actual parameters of an actual parameter list ARE evaluated in the order of their appearance.
requirements.original: The actual parameters are evaluated in the order of their appearance.

requirements.subject: ent:out-parameter
requirements.condition: no actual parameter is provided for an out formal parameter
requirements.canonical: If no actual parameter is provided for an out formal parameter, the dash symbol "-" IS taken as the actual parameter.
requirements.original: If for some formal parameters, no actual parameter has been provided, if they are out parameters, the dash symbol "-" and for in parameters their default values are taken.

requirements.subject: ent:in-parameter
requirements.condition: no actual parameter is provided for an in formal parameter
requirements.canonical: If no actual parameter is provided for an in formal parameter, the default value of the in formal parameter IS taken as the actual parameter.
requirements.original: If for some formal parameters, no actual parameter has been provided, if they are out parameters, the dash symbol "-" and for in parameters their default values are taken.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The default values of formal parameters ARE evaluated after the evaluation of the actual parameters.
requirements.original: Default values are evaluated after the evaluation of the actual parameters and the order of their evaluation corresponds to their order in the formal parameter list.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The default values of formal parameters ARE evaluated in the order of their formal parameters in the formal parameter list.
requirements.original: Default values are evaluated after the evaluation of the actual parameters and the order of their evaluation corresponds to their order in the formal parameter list.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.condition: assignment notation is used
requirements.canonical: If assignment notation is used for the actual parameter list, the order of evaluation of the actual parameters CAN differ from the order of the formal parameters in the formal parameter list.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: If assignment notation has been used for the actual parameter list, the order of the evaluation of actual parameters may differ from the order of the parameters in the formal parameter list.

requirements.subject: ent:empty-parentheses
requirements.condition: all formal parameters of the template have default values and no actual parameters are provided
requirements.canonical: The empty parentheses of an instance of a parameterized template whose formal parameters all have default values MAY be omitted when no actual parameters are provided.
requirements.original: The empty brackets for instances of parameterized templates that have only parameters with default values are optional when no actual parameters are provided, i.e. all formal parameters use their default values.

ambiguity.issue: 'brackets' is used for the parentheses '(' ')' of the actual parameter list.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter-list
requirements.condition: list notation is used
requirements.canonical: When list notation is used, the order of the actual parameters in the actual parameter list SHALL be the same as the order of the formal parameters in the corresponding formal parameter list.
requirements.original: a) When using list notation, the order of elements in the actual parameter list shall be the same as their order in the corresponding formal parameter list.

requirements.subject: ent:inout-parameter
requirements.condition: list notation is used
requirements.canonical: When list notation is used, an actual parameter SHALL be provided for each inout formal parameter.
requirements.original: For each formal inout parameter and for each in parameter without a default there shall be an actual parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:in-parameter
requirements.condition: list notation is used and the in formal parameter has no default value
requirements.canonical: When list notation is used, an actual parameter SHALL be provided for each in formal parameter without a default value.
requirements.original: For each formal inout parameter and for each in parameter without a default there shall be an actual parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:dash-symbol
requirements.canonical: The actual parameter for an out formal parameter or for an in formal parameter with a default value MAY be skipped by using the dash symbol "-" as actual parameter.
requirements.original: The actual parameter of a formal out parameter or in parameter with default value can be skipped by using dash "-" as actual parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: no other actual parameter follows in the actual parameter list
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter MAY be skipped by leaving it out if no other actual parameter follows in the actual parameter list, either because the formal parameter is the last one or because all following formal parameters are out parameters or have default values and are left out.
requirements.original: An actual parameter can also be skipped by just leaving it out if no other actual parameter follows in the actual parameter list - either because the parameter is last or because all following formal parameters are out parameters or have default values and are left out.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter-list
requirements.condition: list notation is used
requirements.canonical: The number of actual parameters in list notation SHALL NOT exceed the number of formal parameters in the formal parameter list.
requirements.original: The number of actual parameters in the list notation shall not exceed the number of parameters in the formal parameter list.

ambiguity.issue: 'parameters in the formal parameter list' means formal parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.condition: assignment notation is used
requirements.canonical: When assignment notation is used, each formal parameter SHALL be assigned an actual parameter at most once.
requirements.original: c) When using assignment notation, each formal parameter shall be assigned an actual parameter at most once.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: assignment notation is used
requirements.canonical: When assignment notation is used, a formal parameter with the same name SHALL exist for each assigned actual parameter.
requirements.original: For each assigned actual parameter there shall exist a corresponding formal parameter of the same name.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.condition: assignment notation is used and the formal parameter has no default value
requirements.canonical: When assignment notation is used, an actual parameter SHALL be provided for each formal parameter without a default value.
requirements.original: For each formal parameter without default value, there shall be an actual parameter.

ambiguity.issue: The rule conflicts with clause 5.4.2 text stating that no actual parameter is needed for out parameters (EXAMPLE 10: f_skip(p_par2 := -) omits out parameter p_par1). Chosen reading: the rule applies to in and inout formal parameters only.
readings: When assignment notation is used, an actual parameter SHALL be provided for each in or inout formal parameter without a default value.
When assignment notation is used, an actual parameter SHALL be provided for each formal parameter without a default value, including out parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: assignment notation is used and the default value of the formal parameter is to be used
requirements.canonical: When assignment notation is used and the default value of a formal parameter is to be used, an assignment for that formal parameter SHALL NOT be provided.
requirements.original: In order to use the default value of a formal parameter, no assignment for this specific parameter shall be provided.

ambiguity.issue: EXAMPLE 10 uses 'f_skip(p_par2 := -)' to obtain the default value, which is an assignment for that parameter. Chosen reading: assigning a real actual parameter is forbidden, assigning "-" is allowed.
readings: When assignment notation is used, a formal parameter that is to take its default value SHALL NOT be assigned an actual parameter other than "-".
When assignment notation is used, a formal parameter that is to take its default value SHALL NOT appear in the assignment list at all.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal parameter is an in parameter
requirements.canonical: The type of an actual parameter for an in formal parameter SHALL be compatible with the type of the formal parameter.
requirements.original: d) For in formal parameters, the type of the actual parameter shall be compatible with the type of the formal parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:out-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal parameter is an out parameter
requirements.canonical: The type of an out formal parameter SHALL be compatible with the type of the actual parameter.
requirements.original: For out formal parameters, the type of the formal parameter shall be compatible with the type of the actual parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:inout-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal parameter is an inout parameter
requirements.canonical: The type of an actual parameter for an inout formal parameter SHALL fulfil strong typing with respect to the type of the formal parameter.
requirements.original: Strong typing is required for inout formal (parameters passed by reference).

ambiguity.issue: 'inout formal (parameters passed by reference)' is a garbled phrase for 'inout formal parameters'.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal parameter is an in formal template parameter
requirements.canonical: The template restriction of an actual parameter for an in formal template parameter SHALL NOT be less restrictive than the template restriction of the formal parameter.
requirements.original: For in formal template parameters, the template restriction of the actual parameter shall not be less restrictive than the one of the formal parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal parameter is an out formal template parameter
requirements.canonical: The template restriction of an actual parameter for an out formal template parameter SHALL NOT be more restrictive than the template restriction of the formal parameter.
requirements.original: For out formal template parameters, the template restriction of the actual parameter shall not be more restrictive than the one of the formal parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal parameter is an inout formal template parameter
requirements.canonical: The template restriction of an actual parameter for an inout formal template parameter SHALL be the same as the template restriction of the formal parameter.
requirements.original: For inout formal template parameters, the template restriction of the actual and the formal parameter shall be the same.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal template parameter has a template restriction
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter passed to a restricted formal template parameter SHALL obey the restrictions given in clause 15.8.
requirements.original: e) Actual parameters passed to restricted formal template parameters shall obey the restrictions given in clause 15.8.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the actual parameter is a parameterized entity
requirements.canonical: A parameterized entity specified as an actual parameter SHALL have its own actual parameters provided in the top-level actual parameter list.
requirements.original: f) All parameterized entities specified as an actual parameter shall have their own parameters resolved in the top-level actual parameter list.

ambiguity.issue: 'resolved in the top-level actual parameter list' can mean that the nested actual parameters are written inline at the point of passing, or that they are taken from the outer parameter list. Chosen reading (EXAMPLE 6): the nested actual parameter list is given inline.
readings: A parameterized entity specified as an actual parameter SHALL be given with its own complete actual parameter list at the place where it is passed.
A parameterized entity specified as an actual parameter SHALL have its formal parameters bound only to actual parameters of the enclosing (top-level) invocation.

requirements.subject: ent:empty-parentheses
requirements.condition: the formal parameter list is empty
requirements.canonical: If the formal parameter list of a function, testcase, altstep or external function is empty, empty parentheses SHALL be included in the declaration of that object.
requirements.original: g) If the formal parameter list of TTCN-3 objects function, testcase, altstep or external function is empty, then the empty parentheses shall be included both in the declaration and in the invocation of that object.

requirements.subject: ent:empty-parentheses
requirements.condition: the formal parameter list is empty
requirements.canonical: If the formal parameter list of a function, testcase, altstep or external function is empty, empty parentheses SHALL be included in each invocation of that object.
requirements.original: g) If the formal parameter list of TTCN-3 objects function, testcase, altstep or external function is empty, then the empty parentheses shall be included both in the declaration and in the invocation of that object.

requirements.subject: ent:empty-parentheses
requirements.condition: the object has an empty formal parameter list and is not a function, testcase, altstep or external function
requirements.canonical: Empty parentheses SHALL be omitted in the declaration and invocation of an object with an empty formal parameter list that is not a function, testcase, altstep or external function.
requirements.original: In all other cases the empty parentheses shall be omitted.

ambiguity.issue: 'In all other cases' may mean all other kinds of objects with an empty formal parameter list, or every case other than the one stated, which would contradict the permission to omit (implying also the permission to keep) parentheses for templates whose formal parameters all have defaults.
readings: Empty parentheses SHALL be omitted for objects without formal parameters other than functions, testcases, altsteps and external functions (e.g. non-parameterized templates).
Empty parentheses SHALL be omitted in every other situation, including instances of parameterized templates whose formal parameters all take default values.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: no other clause specifies differently
requirements.canonical: Unless specified differently in the relevant clause, an actual parameter passed to an in or inout formal parameter SHALL be at least partially initialized.
requirements.original: j) Unless specified differently in the relevant clause(s), actual parameters passed to in or inout formal parameters shall be at least partially initialized (for an exemption see e.g. clause 16.1.2).

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.condition: the function is called within an actual parameter passed to a fuzzy or lazy formal parameter
requirements.canonical: A function called by an actual parameter passed to a fuzzy or lazy formal parameter SHALL NOT have inout or out formal parameters.
requirements.original: k) Functions, called by actual parameters passed to fuzzy or lazy formal parameters of the calling function, shall not have inout or out formal parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function called by an actual parameter passed to a fuzzy or lazy formal parameter MAY internally call other functions that have inout or out formal parameters.
requirements.original: The called functions may use other functions with inout or out parameters internally.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter passed to an out or inout formal parameter SHALL NOT be a reference to a lazy or fuzzy variable.
requirements.original: l) Actual parameters passed to out and inout parameters shall not be references to lazy or fuzzy variables.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: a structured value or template is passed to an inout formal parameter
requirements.canonical: If a value or template of a record, set, union, record of, set of, array or anytype type is passed as an actual parameter to an inout formal parameter, no field or element of that structured value or template SHALL be passed as an actual parameter to another inout formal parameter of the same parameterized TTCN-3 object.
requirements.original: m) Whenever a value or template of a record, set, union, record of, set of, array and anytype type is passed as an actual parameter to an inout parameter, none of the fields or elements of this structured value or template shall be passed as an actual parameter to another inout parameter of the same parameterized TTCN-3 object.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: The prohibition on passing fields or elements of a structured value or template passed to an inout formal parameter to another inout formal parameter of the same object applies recursively to all sub-elements at any level of nesting.
requirements.original: This restriction applies recursively to all sub-elements of the structured value or template in any level of nesting.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: two or more inout actual parameters reference distinct alternatives of the same union or anytype value
requirements.canonical: If two or more actual parameters passed to inout formal parameters of the same parameterized TTCN-3 object contain references to distinct alternatives of the same union or anytype value, a TTCN-3 tool SHALL produce an error.
requirements.original: n) If two or more actual parameters passed to inout parameters of the same parameterized TTCN-3 object contain a reference to distinct alternatives of the same union or anytype value, an error shall be produced.

requirements.subject: ent:mixed-notation
requirements.condition: mixed notation is used
requirements.canonical: If mixed notation is used, list notation SHALL NOT be used for any actual parameter following the first actual parameter in assignment notation.
requirements.original: o) If the mixed notation is used, no value list notation shall be used following the first assignment notation and the parameters given in assignment notation shall not assign parameters that already have an actual parameter given in list notation.

requirements.subject: ent:mixed-notation
requirements.condition: mixed notation is used
requirements.canonical: If mixed notation is used, an actual parameter given in assignment notation SHALL NOT assign a formal parameter that already has an actual parameter given in list notation.
requirements.original: o) If the mixed notation is used, no value list notation shall be used following the first assignment notation and the parameters given in assignment notation shall not assign parameters that already have an actual parameter given in list notation.

ambiguity.issue: 'value list notation' is used for the list notation of actual parameter lists; the glossary term denotes a notation for values of structured types.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal parameter is a @deterministic fuzzy or lazy formal parameter
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter passed to a @deterministic fuzzy or lazy formal parameter SHALL fulfil the restrictions imposed on the content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.original: p) Actual parameters passed to @deterministic fuzzy or lazy formal parameters shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: The final formal parameter of a template, function, external function, altstep or testcase MAY have an ellipsis suffix.
requirements.original: The final formal parameter of a template, function, external `function, altstep or testcase may` have a suffix with … (ellipsis).

requirements.subject: ent:variadic-parameter
requirements.canonical: A final formal parameter with an ellipsis suffix IS called a variadic parameter.
requirements.original: Such formal parameter is called variadic parameter and accepts zero or more values of the specified type.

requirements.subject: ent:variadic-parameter
requirements.canonical: A variadic parameter accepts zero or more values of the specified type.
requirements.original: Such formal parameter is called variadic parameter and accepts zero or more values of the specified type.

requirements.subject: ent:variadic-parameter
requirements.canonical: Inside the parameterized scope, the type of a variadic formal parameter IS a record of the specified type.
requirements.original: Inside the parameterized scope, the type of the formal variadic parameter is a record of the specified type.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: list notation is used
requirements.canonical: When list notation is used, the actual parameter for a variadic formal parameter MAY be absent from the actual parameter list or skipped by using the dash symbol.
requirements.original: The actual parameter is not present in the list of actual parameters or skipped by using the dash symbol.

requirements.subject: ent:variadic-parameter
requirements.condition: the actual parameter for the variadic parameter is absent or skipped
requirements.canonical: If the actual parameter for a variadic formal parameter is absent or skipped, the actual parameter IS equal to an empty record of value or template.
requirements.original: The actual parameter is equal to an empty record of value or template in this case.

ambiguity.issue: EXAMPLE f6 shows that a skipped variadic parameter with a default value takes the default ({1,2,3}) instead of an empty record of. Chosen reading: the empty record of applies when no default value is defined.
readings: If the actual parameter for a variadic formal parameter without default value is absent or skipped, it IS equal to an empty record of value or template.
If the actual parameter for any variadic formal parameter is absent or skipped, it IS equal to an empty record of value or template, even if a default value is defined.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: list notation is used
requirements.canonical: When list notation is used, 1 to N comma-separated values of the specified type MAY be given as the actual parameter for a variadic formal parameter.
requirements.original: Using 1..N comma-separated values of the specified type as the actual parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:variadic-parameter
requirements.canonical: If comma-separated values are given for a variadic formal parameter, the actual parameter IS equal to a record of value or template that contains all the comma-separated values in their order of appearance.
requirements.original: The actual parameter is equal to a record of value or template that contains all the comma-separated values in their declaration order.

ambiguity.issue: 'declaration order' is used for the order in which the values appear in the actual parameter list.

improper_terms.proper: order of appearance in the actual parameter list

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: list notation is used
requirements.canonical: When list notation is used, a single actual parameter of a compatible record of the specified type followed by an ellipsis MAY be given for a variadic formal parameter.
requirements.original: Using a single parameter of a compatible record of the specified type followed by ....

requirements.subject: ent:variadic-parameter
requirements.canonical: If a record of actual parameter followed by an ellipsis is given for a variadic formal parameter, the actual parameter IS passed directly to the variadic formal parameter.
requirements.original: The actual parameter is passed directly to the formal variadic parameter in this case.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: assignment notation is used for the variadic parameter
requirements.canonical: When assignment notation is used for a variadic parameter, the actual parameter SHALL be a value or template of a compatible record of the specified type without an ellipsis.
requirements.original: When using the assignment notation for an actual variadic parameter, the actual parameter shall be a value or template of a compatible record of the specified type without any additional ellipsis.

requirements.subject: ent:variadic-parameter
requirements.condition: assignment notation is used
requirements.canonical: When assignment notation is used for a variadic parameter, the actual parameter IS passed directly to the variadic formal parameter.
requirements.original: The actual parameter is passed directly to the formal variadic parameter in this case.

requirements.subject: ent:variadic-parameter
requirements.canonical: A variadic formal parameter SHALL be an in parameter.
requirements.original: a) The variadic formal parameter shall be an in parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:variadic-parameter
requirements.canonical: A variadic formal parameter SHALL NOT have inout or out parameterization.
requirements.original: Using of inout or out kind of parameterization for variadic parameters is forbidden.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL produce an error if the ellipsis is used in the declaration of a formal parameter that is not the last in the formal parameter list.
requirements.original: b) Using the ellipsis in a declaration of a formal parameter that is not the last in the list of parameters shall produce an error.

requirements.subject: ent:cyclic-definition
requirements.canonical: A direct or indirect cyclic definition SHALL NOT be used, except for recursive type definitions, recursive function or altstep definitions, and cyclic imports that form only allowed cyclic definitions.
requirements.original: Direct and indirect cyclic definitions are not allowed with the exception of the following cases:

requirements.subject: ent:recursive-type-definition
requirements.canonical: A type definition MAY be recursive (cyclic).
requirements.original: a) for recursive type definitions (see clause 6.2);

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function or altstep definition MAY be cyclic, i.e. functions and altsteps MAY be called recursively.
requirements.original: b) function and altstep definitions (i.e. recursive function or altstep calls);

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Import definitions MAY be cyclic if the imported definitions form only allowed cyclic definitions.
requirements.original: c) cyclic import definitions, if the imported definitions only form allowed cyclic definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:cyclic-definition
requirements.canonical: An indirect cyclic definition CAN result from imports of definitions that are needed for the usage of a definition but need not be known in the importing module.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Indirect cyclic definitions may be a result of imports of definitions that are needed for the usage of a definition but do not need to be known in the importing module (see clause 8.2.3.1).
